sources.title: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (2007), Beginners' Guide to Financial Statement
sources.use: Dated investor-education orientation to balance sheets, income statements, cash-flow statements, equity changes and explanatory notes. Harbor's recognition conventions and numerical cases are original and separately stipulated.
sources.verification: Actual official HTML body inspected, principal statements and their connections, balance-sheet equation, period-versus-date distinction and notes discussion. Page reports February 2007 publication/update. Used as elementary orientation, not a current accounting standard. The chapter does not adopt the guide's informal liquidation shorthand as an equality between recorded equity and realizable sale proceeds, or describe all expenses as contemporaneous cash payments.
sources.current_chapter_use: Dated elementary statement connections only; case-specific recognition rules separately stipulated.
sources.current_inspection: Author v15_support_review read retained source scope and accepted prerequisite content; no fresh body retrieval. Original named inspector not specified in retained source record; not inferred.

sources.title: Andrew W. Lo, MIT 15.401 Finance Theory I — Lectures 18–20: Capital Budgeting (2007–2008)
sources.use: NPV choice, incremental after-tax cash and working capital, project interactions, IRR limitations and risk/date matching.
sources.verification: Actual official 37-page PDF text inspected: slides 3–10, 18, 20–31 and 34–35. Some equation glyphs are absent from extracted text; chapter formulas and original numerical cases were independently derived and checked rather than attributed to unseen glyphs. Dated market beta examples and historical survey statistics are not reused. No copied exercises or universal current-tax claim.
sources.current_chapter_use: Incremental dated capital cash, opportunity cost and separate feasibility; original project streams.

sources.title: Marc Farag, Damian Harland and Dan Nixon — Bank capital and liquidity (Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin, 2013 Q3, pp. 201–215)
sources.use: Historical UK central-bank conceptual primer for bank balance-sheet funding, equity versus deployable cash, valuation bases and high-level ratio denominators. Original chapter ledger, definitions, calculations and exercises supply their own assumptions.
sources.verification: Opened official landing page dated 17 September 2013 and actual 15-page PDF. Read printed pp. 201–206 (balance-sheet assets/funding, loss absorption, capital/liquidity distinction, accounting and valuation box), liquidity discussion p. 207 and high-level ratio comparison p. 209. The 2013 incurred-loss timing, then-proposed accounting changes, deposit-protection limits and regulatory thresholds are deliberately excluded from current claims. No source numerical example is reproduced.
sources.current_chapter_use: Conceptual book equity versus cash and balance-sheet reconciliation, excluding historical regulation/accounting requirements.
